method: Individual contextual review of all 82 PDF paragraphs on pages 16–20, including fragments, attribution and potentially misleading ordinary-word combinations.
phrases: in question
being discussed or referred to
所说的；相关的
The document in question was sent yesterday.
所说的那份文件是昨天发送的。
Patient in question identifies the patient under discussion; not a patient asking a question.
no recollection of
no memory of something
对……毫无记忆
I have no recollection of signing that form.
我完全不记得签过那张表。
Of can be followed by a noun or -ing; attributed lack of memory is not independent confirmation of an event.
to put it simply
to explain something in less complicated words
简单地说
To put it simply, we need more time.
简单地说，我们需要更多时间。
Put means express; transferable to ordinary explanations without reproducing the medical-risk context.
gone wrong
developed badly or failed to happen as intended
出了岔子；发生了不良后果
The trip had gone wrong before we even left town.
我们还没离开城镇，这趟旅行就已经出了岔子。
Postmodifier branding gone wrong; teaching example transfers the outcome meaning.
looking into
investigating or trying to learn more about something
调查；深入了解
We are looking into the cause of the delay.
我们正在调查延误的原因。
Not physically looking inside a container.
way more often
much more frequently
频繁得多
We use this room way more often now.
我们现在使用这个房间的频率高多了。
Way is an informal degree intensifier, not a path.
bottom line
the financial result or practical financial interest
财务结果；经济利益
The extra costs will affect our bottom line.
这些额外成本会影响我们的财务结果。
In bottom line incentive, means financial motive rather than the lowest printed line or personal boundary.
alma maters
schools or universities that people formerly attended
母校（复数）
The graduates donated books to their alma maters.
毕业生们向各自的母校捐赠了书籍。
Latin-derived fixed expression; alumni is people, alma maters is their former institutions.
coming up
being raised or appearing in discussion
被提出；出现
The same question keeps coming up in meetings.
同一个问题在会议中不断被提出。
Question emerging in discussion, not an upcoming physical movement.
segments: Dense attributed account includes rammed in the head, full pledged, and same party on the same plan. Full pledged may be nonstandard/ASR; lack of coverage must not be converted into inability to sue.
Speaker's can't sue them inference is not logically established by the preceding insurance exclusion claim. Explain the modal as the speaker's conclusion, not an actual legal prohibition.
Sample is a subset of insurance claims, analyzed by kind; does insure emphasizes an insurer that actually offers this protection. Sample does not represent all possible incidents automatically.
Them refers to claims; categorizing groups them by type, not proving their truth.
Immediately assumed ranking; sentence continues in 246. Assumed here means supposed, unlike assume liability in Unit 4.
Completes possible first/second rankings from 245; right seeks agreement, not a confirmed statistic.
Considering gives a reason for the assumption; terrifying news versus terrorizing newcomers distinguishes fear caused by reports from the actions reported.
Was rushed to hospital is urgent passive transport; like introduces an example rather than similarity.
Initially thought labels a preliminary suspicion; SA'd is an abbreviation/euphemistic rendering of sexually assaulted, not a confirmed finding.
Causative having someone do something plus plastic hoses and explicit anatomy still create barriers. Allegedly is a self-correction limiting the assertion; do not teach this as an instruction.
With alcohol completes the preceding alleged nonmedical practice; retain original short fragment and no procedure details added.
Patient in question means the person being discussed; denies explicitly conflicts with the alleged account, so both must be retained.
Bowels/defecated remain concrete vocabulary gaps. May have and indirect evidence indicate inference; the patient's reported lack of memory does not independently establish the narrative.
Super is an informal intensifier of dangerous. Language review preserves warning without providing instructions or assessing an individual exposure.
Because introduces the narrator's explanation; absorb and bypass now explicitly defined. Quicker is informal adverb use; the medical mechanism is not independently verified here.
Gauge means estimate; to put it simply introduces plainer phrasing, and butt is informal anatomy. No measurement or how-to guidance added.
Sustain means suffer, not maintain; tear means rip tissue, not tears from eyes. Very bright-minded is sarcasm, not praise or diagnosis.
Future of our nation is sarcastic commentary following 257; they say is a generic distancing phrase, not a named source.
Fragmented headline-like wording includes ER and alleged injury; bright-eyed is ironic. Do not reconstruct omitted punctuation into a verified quotation or teach the fragment as standard grammar.
Contrasts initial expectation with a sample ranking; biggest type means most frequent category here, not largest individual legal case.
Assault and battery is a paired violence-related category; battery is not electricity. From this sample limits the comparison, with no jurisdiction-specific legal ruling.
Essay is likely a euphemism or ASR rendering of SA in this list. Preserve the PDF, avoid teaching written essay as a lawsuit category, and await audio verification.
Fixed injury/claim category; not two unrelated actions in a new narrative.
Tied with fifth means equal rank, not physically tied. Auto accidents and sample percentage interpretation need explicit support; no general incident prevalence inferred.
Brief evaluative reaction to the ranking, not independent endorsement.
That's not saying that there aren't... rejects the inference that a lower rank means few lawsuits. Double negatives have a specific logical scope.
Branding is physical marking, not marketing; skin grafts are tissue repair. Extreme cases qualifies severity; teaching examples do not supply injury instructions.
Paddling and aesthetic remain gaps; bottom refers to buttocks rather than a financial bottom line. Distinguish physical appearance from emotional effects.
Light side means supposedly less severe end of the spectrum, not illumination or humor; irony and minimization need an explicit note/card.
Abandoned there is fragment, followed by a new construction in 271. No missing words inferred.
Paddles are flat implements used for hitting in the account, not rowing activity. On there refers to written organization names; needs concrete vocabulary support.
One-word reaction to the preceding explanation.
phrase:4:it seems to be a thing
Standard means usual; a thing means an existing practice. I don't know if and seems explicitly limit certainty.
Spanking is an attempt to clarify the physical action. A one-word concrete vocabulary gap still needs support.
Affirmative response confirming the previous clarification.
Acknowledgment of the explanation, with no new lexical target.
Repeated affirmative response, with no new lexical target.
Repeats light side as the allegedly less severe category; keep the unresolved figurative meaning connected to 269.
Full-on is an intensifier meaning outright/complete; side means an aspect. The nouns alone do not teach these everyday-word combinations.
Still a small percentage compares a subset with all claims; face lawsuits means have proceedings brought against an organization, not a physical face.
Fourth one refers back to the ranked category in 264; students fall from building locations detailed next.
Looking into means researching; this refers to the falls category, not looking inside a house.
Fall off a roof distinguishes movement from a surface; while intoxicated gives the reported state.
Urinate remains an anatomical vocabulary gap; intoxicated alone is insufficient despite the obvious setting.
Fire escapes and balconies now defined, but bunk bed is another common-word compound needing support. Sequence lists several fall locations rather than one continuous fall.
Way intensifies the frequency comparison with the speaker's expectation; no actual frequency statistic supplied.
High falls is an informal recap of falls from elevated places, not highly ranked statistics.
Rhetorical question uses insurers' supposed reluctance to challenge universities' acceptance; this is an argument, not verification of insurers' behavior.
chunk:4:it doesn't even make any sense
Even intensifies an apparent contradiction; make sense means be understandable, not manufacture something.
Greek life is the fraternity/sorority system, not life in Greece. Students are trying to ban it, not a claim that a ban has taken effect.
Protesting against expresses opposition; keeps means retains the system, not physically holds an object.
One-word request for the reason answered in the next paragraph.
Benefit from means receive advantages; the following paragraphs propose financial mechanisms rather than proving each one.
Question proposes donations as an explanation; plural form recognized from the reviewed headword.
Response affirms the proposed source of benefit without giving verified amounts.
Them refers to donations; not disclosed is not publicly revealed, not automatically illegal.
Some people say and could be qualify a proposed promotional explanation; aspect means side of the issue.
Defy gravity and keg stand are distinct idiomatic/cultural barriers. Do not supply instructions for the hazardous drinking stunt; explain receptively if added.
Comparative attraction to some people; than joins social appeal and the cost of education in a sarcastic contrast, not an endorsement.
Built-in is inherent/already included, not physically installed software or hardware.
Imagined promotional message to a prospective student, not a guaranteed experience.
I see acknowledges understanding, not literal sight.
On top of that adds another reason; bottom line is financial interest, not a boundary or printed location.
Financially limits the type of benefit to money; institutions refers to colleges and universities.
Don't have to indicates no necessity, not prohibition; build and maintain separate construction from upkeep. One random one introduces an overlooked reason.
Prepositional fragment specifies the buildings' purpose in 305; no standalone action invented.
Sororities still needs its own lexical support; one in eight is a proportion attributed to some colleges, not a universal housing statistic.
By means per-unit pricing in the speaker's explanation. Less buildings is retained only in source; standard teaching grammar would use fewer buildings.
Speaker uses plural coverages to mean types of protection; learner model normally uses types of coverage, not an automatic plural rule.
Millions of dollars is the narrator's unverified expenditure claim; just on limits the item of spending to dorm insurance.
Burn down means be destroyed by fire; covered/insured concern financial protection. No guarantee about a specific policy is implied.
Puddle remains a concrete noun gap. Might sue is a possible legal claim, not a conclusion that the school is liable.
That refers to the preceding possible liability; as well adds this risk to property loss. Treat necessity as narrator's explanation, not advice.
Since supplies a claimed reason; chapter houses are local organization housing and reduce need means fewer students need campus rooms.
Admit means accept as students; more tuition means increased fee revenue, not more lectures. Which means links the proposed consequence.
Alumni are former students; alma maters their former schools. Seem/according to one research qualify a claimed association, not causation. Research is normally uncountable.
Coming up means emerging in discussion; profanity intensifies the value question, and the teaching model can omit it.
Worth it weighs benefits against alleged danger; appear to be marks impression, not a proved general condition.
One of the oldest, if not the oldest tentatively strengthens a superlative claim; no historical ranking independently verified.
Apparently limits certainty; merged means combined organizations, not merely cooperated.
Oldest of the three selects within the prior group; date is a quoted historical claim and remains unchanged.
Approximate age calculation relative to the recording date, not a request to update the transcript to today's date.
